industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the tape's disagreement now the loudest in the table and the row named as the likeliest source of the tilt scorecard's negative spread. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: C now, D prior at the industry, with Hotels A, Online retail A, Physical retail B and Apparel B: the market is buying the European consumer. The reasons that set F (United States consumer surveys falling, the European consumer never read, a regime that sells discretionary spend) could not be re-tested: no consumer survey for any G10 country was in window this week. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Held because nothing on the causes side changed and a move on the tape alone against two unread legs would be a moved goalpost; the exceptions stay at sector level (Physical retail C). Counter-case: a double notch on 138 stocks against four sectors at A or B on relative strength shuts bottom-up work out of the Lists for the industry where cheap good businesses accumulate, and eight weeks of negative tilt spreads are consistent with this row being wrong. To D on a European consumer reading that is not falling, or a second industry reading at C or better with Hotels and Online retail holding A.

memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage Assessment, medium conviction, explicitly conditional on four named gates. Decision grade [C]. The memo does not recommend park, but names four park triggers so the call is reversible without re-reading the file. The four progression gates: (1) reconcile record game rounds against flat invoiced revenue by building a commission-per-game-round series for Q4-25 to Q2-26; (2) independently verify the disputed live-casino market-share claim, which currently rests on a competitor employee's lobby estimate; (3) quantify how much of the EUR 2.0bn buyback the 19,922,661-share authorisation actually permits at prevailing prices; (4) model the European ring-fencing downside if seven ring-fenced states become fourteen, using the EUR 110m annualised headwind as the base unit. The memo explicitly ADOPTS the Risks report's own stage call rather than beating it. That report says: "The investment case progression recommendation is HOLD-AND-WATCH with conditional re-triggers tied to organic revenue trajectory inflection", described as active surveillance with defined re-entry and exit thresholds rather than immediate capital deployment or permanent rejection. The memo's reasoning: progressing to Early-Stage Assessment is the Viewforth funnel's version of active surveillance, because it commissions deeper research and not a position, so the two recommendations agree in substance. The memo departs from the Risks report on one point only, the regulated-mix leg of the false-friend argument (see COUNTER-CASE). Two downstream actions, both owned by the Investment Analyst, both due 25 August 2026: open the Early-Stage Assessment work plan carrying the four gates as explicit pre-conditions on the Element grades; brief the Researcher for an independent live-casino share check and a European ring-fencing scope update.
case: The memo's argument runs in five steps.

Step one: the change forces are unusually large and unusually self-directed. Nine distinct internal changes fired inside eighteen months: a EUR 2.0bn buyback worth roughly a sixth of market value, a dividend cut to zero after a decade of at least 50% payout, a first-ever revolving credit facility breaking a zero-debt posture, full operational autonomy for the slot division, an exclusive worldwide Hasbro licence producing MONOPOLY Roulette and MONOPOLY Roll'em with eight titles weighted to the second half of 2026, the Galaxy Gaming termination, geographic studio diversification away from Georgia, a rebalanced Asian anti-piracy posture, and a shareholder crossing 32.04% of votes. Against the peer set, only Coloplast's credibility reset is comparable in scale, and Evolution's capital-allocation change is larger.

Step two: the financial base that has to survive the transition is exceptional. EUR 1,153.5m of cash, zero net financial debt, 92% conversion of FY25 adjusted EBITDA into operating cash, and a 65.9% Q2-26 EBITDA margin that exceeded 65% across all sixteen reported periods. Element E8 RA2 CQ3, one-to-many scalability, is the memo's only A grade: a 65.9% EBITDA margin against a 32.6% sector median puts Evolution more than 33 percentage points ahead, described in the source material as the top 2% of business-to-business gaming suppliers globally, and personnel costs fell 1.4% year on year while revenue was flat.
counter_case: The memo carries the counter-case at full force in four strands and does not soften any of them.

Strand one, the Risks report's own verdict. Its competing-hypothesis matrix evaluated 16 evidence items, seven of them diagnostic, and returned FALSE FRIEND as the winning profile with zero hard inconsistencies and one soft, against three hard plus four soft for the pure-bull YES profile and six hard for the outright-failure NO profile. Its stage recommendation is HOLD-AND-WATCH, not proceed. The memo quotes it and adopts it.
triggers: The six ranked questions for Early-Stage Assessment. One: is the gap between record game rounds and flat revenue temporary conversion friction or permanent leakage to unlicensed mirrors. Two: can the 66% EBITDA margin floor hold through the second half of 2026, given the first half printed 65.6%. Three: does European ring-fencing widen beyond seven states, and what is the euro cost per additional state. Four: does the second-half Hasbro slate, including Game Night and MONOPOLY Filthy Rich, produce measurable game-round acceleration. Five: does the slot division sustain double-digit growth beyond the single 14.0% print, or was that a comparison-base effect. Six: what is Kenneth Dart's intent at 32.04% of votes, given no board seats, no public demands and a mandatory-bid trigger already passed.

Park triggers, any of which would force the verdict to park. EBITDA margin below 65.9% for two consecutive quarters absent transitory studio start-up costs, which is the Risks report's own first exit trigger. Unlicensed operator domain-blocking lists expanding by more than 30% year on year across core Western European jurisdictions, validating the regulatory-moat falsification. Tier-one operators successfully piloting synthetic dealer solutions in secondary regulated jurisdictions with positive player retention. Commission per game round falling for three consecutive quarters, which would convert the leakage hypothesis into a structural finding.

Conviction-raising trigger. Two consecutive quarters of constant-currency live revenue growth above 10% without buyback support, which is the Risks report's own upgrade trigger for moving from HOLD-AND-WATCH to PROCEED.
Conviction-lowering trigger. Any evidence that commission per game round is structurally falling, since that single series separates a clearing event from an impairment.

Element-level monitoring items. E5.RA2 moves from C to D on synthetic-dealer regulatory approval in any Tier-1 jurisdiction. E7.RA5 is tested against the next two prints, specifically whether the about-66% margin floor holds through the second half of 2026. E8's carve-out at Early-Stage Assessment deepens RA5 and RA3 at the elevated floor, with RA8 retained as a standing falsification test rather than retired.
Watchlist placement if parked: active watchlist with quarterly review, anchored on the third-quarter and fourth-quarter prints, because the falsification evidence arrives on a quarterly cadence.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
